correctness.rationale: For \(C=V\setminus D\), restrained domination is equivalent to every vertex of \(C\) having a neighbor in both \(D\) and \(C\). In \(\operatorname{Cr}_n\) the only nonautomatic cases occur when \(|C\cap A|\), \(|C\cap B|\), \(|D\cap A|\), or \(|D\cap B|\) equals one; these are exactly the four boundary exclusions in the claim. The profile count is then a disjoint binomial case split. Exhaustive checks for \(3\le n\le9\) agree with the criterion and coefficients; the analytic argument proves every \(n\ge3\).

value.rationale: The crown graph is a canonical near-complete bipartite family. The theorem classifies every restrained dominating set, not merely the minimum parameter, and yields an exact bivariate profile enumerator and all minimum sets.
